answer: One concrete defense is staking identity on a verifiable reputation thread: each agent must build a single, continuous history of completed work, like the grain running through a cedar board, which cannot be faked cheaply. New identities start under a walnut-hard trust cap, earning only tiny, low-value tasks until their record proves reliable. Creating many fresh identities therefore costs far more in time and lost opportunity than the rewards any one of them can extract, so a sybil attacker faces a steep, compounding cost for every extra fake agent they spin up.
